chunks: And Ibn Abi Ja'id al-Qummi informed us from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Abdullah ibn Hamduya ibn al-Bara' from Thabit from Ismail from Abdul Alaa, slave of the family of Sam, who said:

I traveled with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and when we arrived at al-Rawha', he looked at its mountain, gazing upon it, and said to me: 'Do you see this mountain? This is a mountain called Radwa, from the mountains of Fars. It loved us, so Allah transferred it to us. Indeed, every tree on it is edible, and it is a good refuge for the fearful, twice. Indeed, the Master of this Affair will have two occultations in it; one is short and the other is long.'

key_terms.الرَّوْحَاءَ: A station on the road between Mecca and Medina
key_terms.رَضْوَى: A famous mountain in Fars, known for its association with the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: The Master of the Affair, a title for Imam al-Mahdi

ai.seo_question: What are the two occultations of Imam Mahdi mentioned in the hadith of Radwa?
ai.summary: In this tradition from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies Mount Radwa in Fars, explaining its miraculous transfer to the vicinity of Medina due to its affection for the Ahl al-Bayt, serving as a sanctuary for the fearful. He then outlines the eschatological timeline of the Mahdi’s occultation (*al-Ghayba*), distinguishing between the minor occultation (*al-Ghayba al-Sughra*) and the major occultation (*al-Ghayba al-Kubra*), a foundational concept in Twelver Shia theology regarding the Imam's hidden presence.
